TO:  Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Adrian Fajardo, Management Analyst
FROM:  Melissa Burke, Deputy City Manager

SUBJECT:  Discussion on Artesia’s participation in the Neighbors Public Service
  App

BACKGROUND
Security cameras are vital to public safety efforts, offering both preventative and
investigative benefits. They provide real-time surveillance capabilities, enhancing the
ability to monitor public spaces and private properties for unusual activities. Footage from
these cameras can serve as crucial evidence in crime detection and prosecution, aiding
law enforcement in their investigative processes.

Neighbors by Ring is a free app designed to help residents connect with their communities
and stay informed about what’s happening around them. The Neighbors App offers a
platform for residents to share footage from their security cameras and other crime
information and receive updates from official sources. Local agencies can interact with
residents on Neighbors using a tool called Neighbors Public Safety Service (NPSS). The
service is free for all users, including public safety agencies.

NPSS facilitates a collaborative digital environment where residents and public safety
agencies share real-time alerts, updates, and safety tips. Local agency users can view
and comment on public Neighbors App posts within their jurisdiction to connect with and
help community members. They can also create posts to provide communities with safety
tips and other information and invite community members to safety events. Agencies can
follow up to let residents know when an incident has been resolved to close the loop.

Public safety agencies can also issue “Requests for Assistance,” enabling community
members to share information or video recordings voluntarily, fostering a collaborative
environment for addressing local safety concerns.

ANALYSIS
NPSS has been instrumental in enhancing safety through community and public safety
agency collaboration, demonstrating success in various communities in reuniting missing
   ITEM 3

persons, assisting in disasters, and resolving crimes. About 25 public safety agencies in
Los Angeles County have joined Neighbors.

Real-world applications of the Neighbors App have demonstrated its potential in various
contexts:
  • In San Bernardino County, a missing person was successfully located and reunited
  with their family following a community alert issued through NPSS.
  • During the Woolsey Fire in LA and Ventura Counties, the Neighbors App provided
  critical real-time updates to affected communities, aiding coordination and
  evacuation efforts.
  • The Duluth Police Department utilized footage from Ring cameras to identify and
  apprehend a suspect involved in car break-ins, showcasing the utility of combining
  digital platforms with traditional policing methods.

Benefits include enhanced situational awareness, quicker incident response, and more
robust community engagement in public safety efforts. This platform could be another tool
for the City’s public safety campaign and would allow the City to leverage innovative
technological solutions to enhance public safety.

Should the Commission be supportive of this participating in the Program, staff will work
closely with the Lakewood Sheriff’s station to implement the system in Artesia and
develop community engagement strategies to encourage residents to download the app.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission discuss and make
a recommendation to support the City’s participation in the Neighbors Public
Service platform.

  CITY OF ARTESIA

DATE:  April 25, 2024

TO:  Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Adrian Fajardo, Management Analyst
FROM:  Melissa Burke, Deputy City Manager

SUBJECT:  Discussion on the Implementation of an Operation Night Light Program

BACKGROUND
The concept of Operation Night Light comes from a crime abatement strategy developed
by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, aimed at reducing nighttime residential
and vehicle burglaries. The program was introduced as a response to the adaptive
behaviors of criminals, who have increasingly shifted their activities to residential areas.

Operation Night Light is grounded on the observation that poorly lit homes and properties
attract unwelcome attention from potential burglars. Criminals are reported to survey
residential neighborhoods from sunset onwards, looking for signs of unoccupied homes,
particularly those lacking exterior or interior lighting. This program encourages community
participation by asking residents to keep their porch lights on from dusk until dawn,
creating an environment less conducive to criminal activities.

This program complements a series of public safety efforts the City has undertaken in
recent years. Notably, these efforts include the Neighborhood Watch program, the
introduction of a security camera rebate initiative to encourage residents to install
surveillance equipment, and the implementation of a robust public safety marketing
campaign. The City’s marketing campaign has effectively utilized social media platforms
and the Artesian to inform and engage the community about safety measures and crime
prevention strategies. Operation Night Light can be the latest addition to the City’s
comprehensive approach to community safety, furthering the City’s commitment to
protecting residents and their properties.

ANALYSIS
Implementing Operation Night Light within the City could offer several benefits:

  1. Enhanced Nighttime Security: By increasing visibility during the night, the program
  could deter criminal activities and make it easier for law enforcement and residents
  to spot suspicious behavior.
   ITEM 4

  2. Community Engagement: Encouraging residents to participate in Operation Night
  Light fosters a sense of community responsibility and involvement in public safety
  efforts. It can also serve as a stepping stone to further engagement with the City’s
  Neighborhood Watch program.
  3. Cost-Effectiveness: The program's simplicity and reliance on residents'
  participation make it a cost-effective method of crime prevention. The use of
  photocell-equipped lighting further reduces the burden on residents by automating
  the process.
  4. Visibility and Deterrence: A well-lit neighborhood sends a clear message to
  potential criminals that the community is vigilant and proactive about security. This
  can have a psychological impact on would-be burglars, potentially reducing crime
  rates.

The Operation Night Light program presents an opportunity to enhance nighttime security
through a simple, community-driven initiative. This program represents a natural
extension of the City’s efforts to create a safer community. It not only strengthens the
City’s existing programs but can also empower residents to contribute to the safety of
their neighborhoods directly.

The program's effectiveness would depend on widespread community participation and
awareness. Should the Commission be supportive of implementing an Operation Night
Light program, we would seek additional guidance on how to promote it through the City’s
various marketing channels.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission recommend implementing an
Operation Night Light Program.

  CITY OF ARTESIA

DATE:  April 25, 2024

TO:  Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Adrian Fajardo, Management Analyst
FROM:  Melissa Burke, Deputy City Manager

SUBJECT:  Receive and File an Update on Automated License Plate Readers

BACKGROUND
In recent years, Los Angeles County has observed an uptick in vehicle-related crimes,
notably vehicle thefts and the use of vehicles in the commission of crimes. This trend
poses significant challenges to public safety and law enforcement efforts, underscoring
the need for innovative and effective surveillance solutions.

In April 2022, the Public Safety Commission briefly discussed the potential
implementation of Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) cameras throughout the
City. Commissioner Nunes suggested the City consider the ALPR cameras from Flock
Group Inc. Since then, the City has explored deploying ALPR cameras and solicited
proposals from Flock and Motorola's Vigilant Solutions. After receiving and evaluating
proposals from both Flock and Vigilant Solutions, it was determined that Vigilant Solutions
offered a more cost-effective solution over time.

Vigilant Solutions has an existing contract with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's
Department. This pre-established relationship presents an opportunity for seamless
integration, enabling the City to easily connect with the broader network of Vigilant ALPR
cameras throughout the County. This network can foster enhanced regional coordination
in public safety operations, leveraging county-wide data for more effective crime
prevention and investigation.

ANALYSIS
The City is proposing deploying ALPR cameras at critical thoroughfares and intersections
within the City. Staff met with Sgt. Ramos and the Advanced Surveillance and Protection
Unit (ASAP) of the Sheriff's Department to carefully identified these specific locations.
These locations have been selected based on traffic patterns, historical crime data, and
the strategic importance of monitoring vehicular movements in and out of the City.
   ITEM 5

The following locations are being considered at this time:
  • Northbound Pioneer Blvd/Artesia Blvd
  • Northbound Pioneer Blvd/South St.
  • Southbound Pioneer Blvd/166th St.
  • Southbound Pioneer Blvd/183rd St.
  • Southbound Pioneer Blvd/
  • Southbound Pioneer Blvd/
  • Southbound Norwalk Blvd/Artesia Blvd
  • Westbound Norwalk Blvd/South St.
  • Westbound Norwalk Blvd/Artesia Blvd
  • Eastbound Artesia Blvd/Gridley Rd.
  • Eastbound 183rd St./Gridley Rd.

After carefully considering and reviewing available options, the City has determined that
the L6Q ALPR Camera from Vigilant Solutions would best suit our needs. The L6Q was
designed with rapid deployment capabilities, a high-capacity swappable internal battery,
and compatibility with solar and AC/DC power sources. Its sophisticated radar-based
triggering system is designed to capture data on vehicles moving at specified speed
thresholds and directions and across multiple lanes. The system includes long-range
integrated infrared illumination and a starlight sensor, enabling effective operation in low-
light conditions.

The L6Q is a powerful tool for enhancing public safety and investigative capabilities. By
capturing detailed data on every vehicle that passes, including license plate, make,
model, color, and speed, deputies can quickly identify stolen vehicles, track suspects,
and gather crucial evidence for investigations.

The adoption of ALPR Cameras offers the City of Artesia significant technological
advantages. These cameras align with the City's goal to enhance public safety by
providing a robust foundation for crime prevention and investigation efforts. Our Sheriff
Deputies will have a critical tool to deter criminal activities and solve crimes more
effectively. This program underscores the City's broader commitment to harnessing
technology to address evolving public safety concerns.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission receive and file an update on the
implementation of Automated License Plate Reader technology.
